transcript.en: Last week, we started looking at reptiles, including crocodiles and snakes.
transcript.zh: 上周，我们开始研究爬行动物，包括鳄鱼和蛇。

transcript.en: Today, I'd like us to have a look at another reptile - the lizard - and in particular,
transcript.zh: 今天，我们将研究另一种爬行动物 - 蜥蜴 -

transcript.en: at some studies that have been done on a particular type of lizard whose Latin name is tiliqua rugosa.
transcript.zh: 特别是，对一种特殊类型的蜥蜴所做的一些研究，这种蜥蜴的拉丁名字是tiliqua rugosa。

transcript.en: This is commonly known as the sleepy lizard, because it's quite slow in its movements and spends quite a lot of its time dozing under rocks or lying in the sun.
transcript.zh: 它通常被称为“瞌睡蜥蜴”，因为它的动作非常缓慢，并且相当多的时间都是在岩石下面或躺在阳光下打瞌睡。

transcript.en: I'll start with a general description.
transcript.zh: 我先大概介绍一下。

transcript.en: Sleepy lizards live in Western and South Australia, where they're quite common.
transcript.zh: “瞌睡蜥蜴”生活在澳大利亚西部和南部，它在这两个地区很常见。

transcript.en: Unlike European lizards, which are mostly small, green and fast- moving sleepy lizards are brown,
transcript.zh: 不像大部分体型小、绿色和移动迅速的欧洲蜥蜴，“瞌睡蜥蜴”身体是棕色的，

transcript.en: but what's particularly distinctive about them is the colour of their tongue, which is dark blue, in contrast with the lining of their mouth which is bright pink.
transcript.zh: 但最明显的区别是它的舌头颜色“深蓝色”与嘴巴里面的粉红色形成鲜明对比

transcript.en: And they're much bigger than most European lizards.
transcript.zh: 而且它们比大多数欧洲蜥蜴都要大得多。

transcript.en: They have quite a varied diet including insects and even small animals, but they mostly eat plants of varying kinds.
transcript.zh: 它们的饮食多种多样，包括昆虫，甚至小动物，但它们大多吃各种各样的植物。

transcript.en: Even though they're quite large and powerful, with strong jaws that can crush beetles and snail shells, they still have quite a few predators.
transcript.zh: 尽管他们体型巨大，并且力量强大，它们的下颌可以压扁甲虫和蜗牛壳，但它们仍然有相当多的捕食者。

transcript.en: Large birds like cassowaries were one of the main ones in the past, but nowadays they're more likely to be caught and killed by snakes.
transcript.zh: 像食火鸡这样的大型鸟类是过去的主要鸟类之一，但现在它们更有可能被蛇捕获并杀死。

transcript.en: Actually, another threat to their survival isn't a predator at all, but is man-made -
transcript.zh: 实际上，他们生存的另一个威胁根本不是捕食者，而是人类

transcript.en: quite a large number of sleepy lizards are killed by cars when they're trying to cross highways.
transcript.zh: 很多瞌睡蜥蜴是在试图穿越高速公路时被汽车压死的

transcript.en: One study carried out by Michael Freake at Flinders University investigated the methods of navigation of these lizards.
transcript.zh: 弗林德斯大学的Michael Freake进行的一项研究调查了这些蜥蜴的导航方法。

transcript.en: Though they move slowly, they can travel quite long distances.
transcript.zh: 虽然它们移动缓慢，但它们可以走很远的距离。

transcript.en: And he found that even if they were taken some distance away from their home territory,
transcript.zh: 而且他发现，即使它们被带离家乡有一段距离，

transcript.en: they could usually find their way back home as long as they could see the sky - they didn't need any other landmarks on the ground.
transcript.zh: 它们通常也能找到回家的路，只要他们能看到天空 - 他们不需要地面上的任何其他地标。

transcript.en: Observations of these lizards in the wild have also revealed that their mating habits are quite unusual.
transcript.zh: 对这些蜥蜴在野外的观察也表明，它们的交配习性是非常不寻常的。

transcript.en: Unlike most animals, it seems that they've relatively monogamous, returning to the same partner year after year.
transcript.zh: 与大多数动物不同，它们似乎相对一夫一妻制，年复一年地回到同一个伴侣身边。

transcript.en: And the male and female also stay together for a long time, both before and after the birth of their young.
transcript.zh: 而且雌雄蜥蜴在它们的幼子出生前后都会长时间呆在一起。

transcript.en: It's quite interesting to think about the possible reasons for this.
transcript.zh: 想一想可能的原因是很有趣的。

transcript.en: It could be that it's to do with protecting their young – you'd expect them to have a much better chance of survival if they have both parents around.
transcript.zh: 这可能与保护他们的幼子有关 - 如果父母都在身边，幼子的生存几率就更高。

transcript.en: But in fact observers have noted that once the babies have hatched out of their eggs, they have hardly any contact with their parents.
transcript.zh: 但事实上，观察人员指出，一旦从卵子里孵化出来，幼子几乎不会与父母有任何接触。

transcript.en: So, there's not really any evidence to support that idea.
transcript.zh: 所以，没有任何证据支持那个观点。

transcript.en: Another suggestion's based on the observation that male lizards in monogamous relationships tend to be bigger and stronger than other males.
transcript.zh: 另一个建议是基于观察到一夫一妻制关系中的雄性蜥蜴往往比其他雄性更大更强壮。

transcript.en: So maybe the male lizards stay around so they can give the female lizards protection from other males.
transcript.zh: 所以也许雄蜥蜴呆在附近，就是为了让雌性蜥蜴免受其他雄性的侵害。

transcript.en: But again. we're not really sure.
transcript.zh: 但是，我们同样并不确定。

transcript.en: Finally, I'd like to mention another study that involved collecting data by tracking the lizards.
transcript.zh: 最后，我想提及另一项涉及通过跟踪蜥蜴来收集数据的研究。

transcript.en: I was actually involved in this myself.
transcript.zh: 我自己也参与其中。

transcript.en: So we caught some lizards in the wild and we developed a tiny GPS system that would allow us to track them, and we fixed this onto their tails.
transcript.zh: 我们把自己开发的一个小型GPS系统安装在它们的尾巴上，以进行跟踪。

transcript.en: Then we set the lizards free again, and we were able to track them for twelve days and gather data,
transcript.zh: 然后我们把蜥蜴放了，跟踪12天后收集数据，

transcript.en: not just about their location, but even about how many steps they took during this period.
transcript.zh: 不仅仅是关于它们的位置，甚至是这段时间它们走了多少步。

transcript.en: One surprising thing we discovered from this is that there were far fewer meetings between lizards than we expected -
transcript.zh: 我们从中发现的一件令人惊讶的事情是，

transcript.en: it seems that they were actually trying to avoid one another.
transcript.zh: 蜥蜴之间的会面比我们想象的要少得多 - 看起来他们实际上是在试图回避对方。

transcript.en: So why would that be? Well, again we have no clear evidence,
transcript.zh: 那这是为什么呢？好吧，我们又没有明确的证据，

transcript.en: but one hypothesis is that male lizards can cause quite serious injuries to one another,
transcript.zh: 但有一个假设是，雄性蜥蜴可能会对彼此造成相当严重的伤害，

transcript.en: so maybe this avoidance is a way of preventing this - of self-preservation, if you like.
transcript.zh: 所以也许这种回避是一种自我保护方式。

transcript.en: But we need to collect a lot more data before we can be sure of any of this.
transcript.zh: 但是我们需要收集更多的数据，然后才能确定这一点。
